label: paragraph_title

label: paragraph_title

label: text
text: DIPLOMACY AND FACT

label: paragraph_title
text: 一

label: text
text: An interesting passenger by the s.s. "President Pierce" which arrived in Hongkong this morning is Dr. Tsun Kit-wong, a native of Canton who for eleven years has been away from his native land studying law in America.

label: text
text: In an interview reproduced in an American newspaper, prior to his departure, Dr. Tsun Kit-wong is credited with having stated that "militarism in China is dying a natural death and the Democratic principles" of "Government based on the American constitution are being firmly rounded. The military leaders in China are fast losing their power, while at the same time the diplomatic Government of Canton is becoming stronger every day. In a very few years Canton will be the seat of a Chinese diplomatic Government based on the American form."

label: text
text: The same paper states that "Dr. Tsun Kit-wong came to America" with the idea of carrying back to his people the methods of Government which have made this nation one of the world's greatest. His ambition is to draft such a Constitution to which it has devoted much study.

label: text
text: "Seen this morning by a China Mail" representative: Dr. Taun Kit-wong stated that it was an entirely new China to which he was returning. He had not studied the political situation sufficiently to express an opinion but it had come as a great surprise to him to learn that on returning after eleven years to visit his father in Canton, so many difficulties in the way of passports from various powers in Canton were necessary.

label: text
text: It is Dr. Tsun Kit-wong's intention, once having visited his father, to go to Shanghai where he intends setting up in practice. He graduated from Canton High School and went to America in 1916, entering the Stockton High School. He graduated from the Baldwin-Wallace College, Ohio and finally from the legal department of the De Paul University of Chicago.

label: paragraph_title
text: "THE " QUAINTS."

label: paragraph_title
text: MISS DORIS WOODS IN INDIA.

label: text
text: HOW OLD FRIENDS FARE.

label: text
text:
Hongkong theatre-goers will be pleased to learn that our old friends—Mr. R. B. Salisbury's "Quaints"—are going great guns in their present tour of India.
Miss Doris Woods, the popular teacher of dancing, who joined the company here, has proved a great success. Her performance as Sue Smith in "No. No. Nanette," has been described as "really splendid." In other parts she has also made a name. A big hit was scored by Miss Doris in "The Quaints" as themselves, in which she introduced many new features.

label: text
text: The company of mirth makers will be in India till December, their itinerary including Calcutta, Bombay, Poona, Karachi, Quetta, Lahore, Meerut, Delhi, Agra, Simla, Rawalpindi, Peshawar, Cawnpore, Lucknow, Allahabad and Jubbulpore.

label: text
text: Quite a number of Hongkong-ites will be pleased to see the "Quaints" return.

label: text
text: Miss Aileen. Woods, sister of Miss Doris, is due back in Hongkong next month. She has been away for over three years and is coming back to carry on her sister's dancing tuition until Miss Doris's return.

label: text
text: This is what the "Times of India" say about the "Quaints":—

label: text
text: "No, No, Nanette" has long since gained a world-wide popularity because of its tunefullness and witty quips, and "quibbles." Few changes have been made in the cast but Doris Woods as Sue Smith was really splendid. Gordon Rennie and R. B. Salisbury make much capital out of the long succession of humorous situations in which they find themselves. The nimbleness of the former and the drollness of the latter kept every one in fits of mirth from start to finish. Ella Erskine was very dainty as "Nanette." She saging and danced well, while Mavis French was funnier than ever as Pauline, Babs Lille, Kathleen West and Doff Dee were splendid in their respective roles, the dancing of Miss West being encored again and again.

label: paragraph_title
text: HEROIN TRAFFIC.

label: text
text:
SEIZURE ON FRENCH MAIL
STEAMER

label: text
text: JAPANESE PLEADS GUILTY,

label: text
text: As a result of the raid by revenue officers on the French mail steamer "Angers" yesterday, a Japanese passenger on the vessel was "charged before Mr. R. E. Lindsell at the Central Magistracy this morning on two counts under the Dangerous Drugs Ordinance".

label: text
text: Johejiro Tanaka, 37 years of age, described as a tailor by profession, pleaded guilty to charges of unlawful possession of 8,200 ounces of heroin and importing the drug.

label: text
text: This record quantity of heroin, packed in cardboard boxes, was found in seven cabin trunks in the baggage room claimed by the defendant, who had booked from Marseilles to Kobe.

label: text
text: At the Home market price, the seizure would be worth more than $100,000, but out here about three times as much.

label: text
text: Mr. J. D. Lloyd (Superintendent of Imports and Exports) asked for a committal of the defendant to the Sessions on both charges.

label: text
text: The case was fixed for hearing at 11:30 a.m. on Saturday.

label: paragraph_title
text: PAPER THEFT.

label: text
text: NANYANG ACCOUNTANT SENT TO PRISON.

label: paragraph_title
text: BOOKS FALSIFIED

label: text
text: Investigations into the books of the Nanyang Brothers Tobacco Company revealed further irregularities committed by a Chinese accountant of the firm who pleaded guilty before Mr. R. E. Lindsell last week to lureny of 70 bales of glassine paper.

label: text
text: When the case was called this morning, Mr. D. L. Strellet added four other charges of larceny of glassine paper and 'tan other' charge of making false entries in the accounts.

label: text
text: Defendant was sentenced to one month's imprisonment on each of the five charges of larceny and to three months' imprisonment on the charge of falsifying the accounts — eight months' hard labour in all.

label: paragraph_title
text: ALI BABA.

label: paragraph_title
text: INDIANS STORY OF GEMS & IDOLS OF GOLD.

label: text
text: New York, July 23.—A weird story of a enve filled with idols made of the purest gold comes from Mexico.

label: text
text: It is related by the director of the National Museum in Mexico City, who has commissioned a party of explorers to seek for the cave, which is situated somewhere in the Santa Clara Mountains.

label: text
text: The director says that some time ago an old Indian visited his office and offered to lead him to the mysterious cave. The man explained that he was a charcoal "burner," and happened to come upon the treasure while seeking shelter from a storm.

label: text
text: Entering a long tunnel, he suddenly found himself in a cave, which was lighted by a ray of light from the roof.

label: text
text: The ray, falling on two huge idols, caused them to shine as the sun, and at first filled him with terror.

label: text
text: The cave, which was of large dimensions (so the man continued), was filled with golden images and armour of gold, set with precious stones.

label: text
text: On leaving the cave the covered the entrance to prevent its rediscovery, and had journeyed to the capital to enlist the assistance of the museum director, whom he offered to lend to the spot.

label: text
text: The director was unable at the time to accompany him. When later he sought the Indian he found that the old man had died.

label: paragraph_title
text: BRITISH SUBJECT FOUND ON SHIP

label: text
text: "LOOKING FOR UNCLE."

label: text
text: Victor Simpson, a British subject, was charged this morning before Mr. J. H. B. Nihill at the Kowloon Magistracy with having had a "free transportation" from Shanghai to Hongkong without the consent of the owners or master of the as. "Linan" of the China Navigation Company.

label: text
text: The defendant, in relating his story to the Magistrate, said that he came from Tsingtao en route to Hongkong via Shanghai with $500 and on arriving at Shanghai all his money was stolen from him. He made several attempts to see the British consul at Shanghai, but the latter postponed his interview several times, while he ran short of funds.

label: text
text: He sold some of his personal belongings to support himself, continued defendant. To continue

label: text
text: his trip to the colony, he appealed to the second officer of the steamer who asked him to wait. According to the defendant, he was so tired that he went to sleep underneath a life-boat while he

label: text
text: waited for the second officer. He did not wake up until the next morning when the steamer was already sailing. A sailor inquired what he was doing on the ship and reported the matter to the master.

label: text
text: In conclusion, defendant told his Worship: "I am looking for my uncle named William Simpson who is staying in Hongkong and I want to find him as he is supposed to look after me."

label: text
text: The master of the "Linan" gave evidence, corroborated the testimony of the defendant as to he circumstances under which he was found.

label: text
text: His Worship, in passing sentence, informed the accused that the regular "penalty" for the charge against him was imprisonment, but that he took into consideration his age (defendant was scarcely twenty) and gave credit to his story, and would not therefore send him to jail.

text:

label: paragraph_title
text: BOBBED HAIR.

label: paragraph_title
text: CRAZE ENDED IN BERLIN.

label: text
text: Berliners, like gentlemen, "prefer blondes."

label: text
text: This is shown (writes the Berlin correspondent of the London "Daily Chronicle." under date of June 10) by the fact that Berlin has chosen a "blondine" as the city's "Summer Queen of Beauty." She is Fraulein Grete Reinwald, a pretty young firm actress.

label: text
text: Fashion journals are more interested in the "fact that the queen" has not bobbed or shingled air.

label: text
text: Little more than a year ago the short hair craze reached here. Almost in a night it captured the fair sex of Berlin.

label: text
text: It was exceedingly unpopular with the male population. Callous employers dismissed their women secretaries, clerks and typists for no other reason than that they had bobbed or shingled hair. Hundreds of engagements must have been broken off for the same reason. Yet, for weeks, there were queues outside the barbers' shops.

label: text
text: But Fraulein Grete's election is a sign of the times. There is little doubt that she was chosen because she had not yielded to the "un-womanly and un-German fashion."

label: text
text: The reaction against short hair has set in with that impetus with which the new fashion originally conquered Berlin. Actresses and film stars are flocking to lonely holiday resorts—determined to come back capable of playing Juliet or Marguerite without false hair.

label: text
text: Though the burber laments that the “ladiés” salon” is now almost deserted, he has begun to do n' roaring business in hair restorers!

label: text

label: paragraph_title
text: OWNERS' ATTITUDE.

label: text
text: Rugby, Sept. 1.

label: text
text: Although no fresh move in the coal dispute is to be expected until after to-morrow's delegate conference, further interviews took place to-day with a view to facilitating direct negotiations.

label: text
text: The Miners' Executive met in the morning and later had a long discussion with Mr. Ramsay MacDonald and other leaders of the Labour Party. Although nothing tangible emerged, importance is attached to this meeting in view of Mr. Winston Churchill's appeal to the miners to formulate fresh proposals.

label: text
text: No report has been issued in regard to the interview of Mr. Churchill "and other members of the Government with the goal owners' organisation. The Government's decision—that the claim of the miners for national negotiations is "reasonable so long as the latter are prepared to advance helpful suggestions as a basis of discussion—was, it is assumed, discussed with the owners.

label: text
text: On the owners' behalf it was recently stated that their central organisation had no longer power to discuss wages and conditions with the Miners' District Associations.

label: text
text: the responsibility for such negotiations. It is not yet known whether this will constitute a definite bar to proceeding with efforts to secure a national settlement.

label: text
text: Meanwhile the miners are returning to work in increasing numbers in the Midlands, and it is reported that Lancashire and Cheshire coal owners have invited the men to discuss a local settlement.—British Wireless Service.

label: paragraph_title

label: paragraph_title
text: SIGNS A TREATY WITH AFGHANISTAN.

label: text
text: NON-AGGRESSIVE PACT.

label: text
text: Moncov, Sept.

label: text
text: A Russo-Afghan Treaty of neutrality and mutual non-aggression has been signed with great ceremony at Pagman, the Summer residence of the King of Afghanistan, by M. Stark, the Soviet Plenipotentiary, and the Afghan Foreign Minister.

label: text
text: It provides for neutrality in the event of an armed conflict between either and third Powers, mutual non-aggression and abstention from entering into hostile agreements with third Powers, and mutual non-interference in home affairs.—Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: NEGROES CUT OFF IN A TENEMENT.

label: paragraph_title
text: LEAP FOR LIFE

label: text
text: Five negroes are dead and one missing as the result of a fire in a five-storey negro tenement, the occupants of which were cut off from escape owing to a deep trench, which was cut in front of the building for a new underground railway, which prevented the fire-men hoisting ladders.

label: text
text: Many of the negroes jumped from the windows and were more or less seriously injured.—Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: TO CONQUER OIL

label: text
text: AIM OF GERMAN CHEMICAL COMBINE.

label: text
text: CAPITAL INCREASED.

label: text
text: Berlin, Sept. 1.

label: text
text: An extraordinary general meeting of the Farbon Industrie Company, namely, the Chemicals Combine approved of an increase of the Company's capital from 640,000,000 marks to 110,000,000 marks.

label: text
text: The Chairman said that the past year had been favourable for the business and financial progress. The Company, which had hitherto been predominant in the nitrogen market, now aimed at conquering the oil market,—Reuter.

label: text

label: text
text: The death is announced of the Chinese Ambassador, Li Kia-no.—Reuter.

label: text
text: [Li Chao-ao, who preferred the name of Li Kia-ao, was born in 1868; studied in Russia at his own expense; practised law and became a judge. He had a long diplomatic career, principally in Russia.]

label: paragraph_title
text: VIOLENT STORM.

label: text
text: LIGHTNING'S HAVOC IN LONDON.

label: text
text: TRAMCAR ON FIRE.

label: text
text: Rugby, Sept. 1.

label: text
text: A brief but violent thunderstorm, which broke over London this morning, did considerable damage. "There were many narrow escapes, but no lives were lost.

label: text
text: The streets in the low-lying localities were flooded, and the electric railway service between the City and Kew was disorganised owing to the current being cut off through the flooding of the track.

label: text
text: The buildings struck included elementary school buildings and ten houses.

label: text
text: Two tramway cars, of which one was set on fire, were also struck, and owing to the floods it became necessary temporarily to change the route of certain bus services.—British Wireless Service.
